discovery: Detection of baryon acoustic oscillations in the large-scale distribution of galaxies, establishing a standard ruler for cosmic expansion

nominees.name: Daniel J. Eisenstein
nominees.affiliation: Harvard University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: Shaun Cole
nominees.affiliation: Durham University, Institute for Computational Cosmology, UK

nominees.name: John A. Peacock
nominees.affiliation: University of Edinburgh, Institute for Astronomy, UK

motivation: In 2005 the SDSS (led in this analysis by Eisenstein) and the 2dF Galaxy Redshift Survey (Cole, Peacock and collaborators) independently detected the baryon acoustic oscillation feature in galaxy clustering: the imprint, frozen into the matter distribution, of sound waves in the primordial photon-baryon plasma. Eisenstein also developed the theoretical framework that made the feature a precise standard ruler. The detection confirmed that structure grew gravitationally from the same fluctuations seen in the cosmic microwave background, within a universe dominated by cold dark matter, and it gave a geometric, systematics-robust measurement of the expansion history. BAO has since become a central probe of dark energy, through BOSS, eBOSS and now DESI, whose 2024-25 results hint that dark energy may evolve with time. This is a fundamental physical discovery about the contents and dynamics of the Universe, linking early-universe physics to today's cosmic web.
